process.title: Bell 数组件 bell.py
process.scope: Owns only bell.py and tests/test_bell.py (both new files). Does not touch tapcode.py, decimaltime.py, or any existing file; no imports beyond the standard library; no imports from the other two modules.
process.task:
Implement the Bell number component exactly to the work order spec, creating only two new files: bell.py and tests/test_bell.py. Do not modify any existing file; use only the standard library; do not import tapcode or decimaltime.

API: bell_number(n: int) -> int returns the n-th Bell number B_n (number of partitions of an n-element set), with B_0 = 1.

Validation (acceptance section, verbatim):
- n must be int; bool is rejected (bool is not accepted even though it is an int subclass).
- Non-int n raises TypeError.
- n < 0 raises ValueError.

Acceptance examples, every one must have a corresponding test case in tests/test_bell.py:
- bell_number(0) == 1
- bell_number(1) == 1
- bell_number(2) == 2
- bell_number(3) == 5
- bell_number(4) == 15
- bell_number(5) == 52
- bell_number(6) == 203
- bell_number(7) == 877
- bell_number(8) == 4140
- bell_number(9) == 21147
- bell_number(10) == 115975
- bell_number(15) == 1382958545
- bell_number(20) == 51724158235372
- bell_number(-1) raises ValueError
- bell_number(2.5), bell_number("5"), bell_number(True) each raise TypeError

Include a test case for each acceptance example above (14 value checks + 4 error checks minimum). Implement B_n via a standard exact-integer algorithm (e.g. triangle/Bell-triangle or Stirling numbers of the second kind); values must be exact for n up to 20.

Checks (run from repository root):
1. python3 -m pytest tests/test_bell.py -q
2. python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
